phase_name: state-write.sh regression test above the 128KB ceiling

objectives.description: Case A: >131072-byte payload in one call exits 0
Case F: --dry-run oversized exits 0, no temp files
Register in run-all.sh if it enumerates top-level test-state-write-*.sh files

deviations.description: Case A: 'generate a fixture with a >131,072-byte JSON array in one call exits 0' via --argjson
deviations.reason: Per the Phase 1 deviation, a >131,072-byte value cannot be passed via literal --argjson at all (state-write.sh's own invocation fails at the OS level, exit 126, before the script runs). Case A instead exercises --argjson-file (the mechanism that genuinely works above the ceiling) with a 200,001-byte file, and a new Case A0 was added that directly proves the OS-level ceiling (exit 126) so a future reader understands why. Case E covers the plain --argjson spill path in its only reachable range (100000, ~131072] bytes.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- Case A uses --argjson-file for genuinely oversized payloads; a new Case A0 proves the OS-level exec ceiling that motivates this. See Phase 1's deviation entry for the full analysis.)*

Confirmed by direct execution: the new suite is discovered and run without any edit to run-all.sh.
